b: Press release by Tata Steel Chess
From 15 to 31 January 2027, Wijk aan Zee will once again welcome the world's chess elite.

The 89th edition of the Tata Steel Chess Tournament (TSCT) will bring together established stars and a new generation of chess talent. Featuring World Championship challenger Javokhir Sindarov, Alireza Firouzja, Vincent Keymer, defending champion Nodirbek Abdusattorov, Anish Giri and Levon Aronian, among others, the Masters once again boasts a formidable lineup.

The Masters field brings together players from different generations. Alongside experienced top players such as Levon Aronian and Anish Giri, the lineup includes young talents such as Yagiz Kaan Erdogmus, Andy Woodward, Nihal Sarin and Frederik Svane. The Netherlands will be represented by Anish Giri and Jorden van Foreest.
Tournament Director Jeroen van den Berg:

Once again, we have a fantastic lineup, with a great mix of established names and young players who are making their mark. It is precisely this combination that makes the Tata Steel Chess Tournament so exciting every year. In Wijk aan Zee, talented players have the opportunity to test themselves at the very highest level, something that has led to many surprises in the past.
Rising star Yagiz Kaan Erdogmus, now aged 15, scored 7/13 in the 2026 edition of the Masters | Photo: Nils Rohde / ChessBase

The Challengers tournament also features a strong international field. Aravindh Chithambaram, Zhu Jiner, Bibisara Assaubayeva, Alice Lee and Nikolas Theodorou are among the players heading to Wijk aan Zee. The Netherlands will be represented by Casper Schoppen and Max Warmerdam.

One particularly noteworthy participant is 17-year-old Ukrainian Ihor Samunenkov. In 2020, at the age of ten, he was already a guest at the Tata Steel Chess Tournament, where he made the ceremonial opening move for one of the rounds during the first weekend. He had won his visit to Wijk aan Zee in a competition held during Judit Polgar's Global Chess Festival. Seven years later, he returns, this time as a grandmaster and a participant in the Challengers tournament. At the 46th Chess Olympiad in Samarkand this autumn, Ihor was one of the standout performers, winning an individual gold medal for Ukraine.

Ihor Samunenkov's return is a wonderful story. In 2020, he came here as a ten-year-old guest, and now he is returning as a participant in the Challengers. It is a great illustration of how quickly young chess talents can develop and how special it is to see players return to Wijk aan Zee at different stages of their careers.
Max Warmerdam | Photo: Nils Rohde / ChessBase

Every year, the Tata Steel Chess Tournament brings together the world's leading chess players, amateurs and chess enthusiasts in Wijk aan Zee. Alongside the grandmaster tournaments, large numbers of amateur players traditionally take part as well. The international chess tournament is widely known as the 'Wimbledon of Chess'.
